text: Europe in 1200

The year 1200 opens a new age. In France, King Philip Augustus presses on the lands of the Angevin family. Richard the Lionheart died in 1199, and his brother John now holds England, Normandy, Anjou and Aquitaine. In Spain the Christian kings quarrel with each other, while the Almohad caliph rules Africa and the south of the peninsula. In Germany two kings fight for one crown. In the south of France, a new faith spreads that Rome calls heresy. Over all of them stands the pope, who says that he judges kings.
The authorities

Innocent III became pope in January 1198, at the age of about 37. He teaches that the pope stands above every king, as the vicar of Christ. He wants to rule the lands of the Church again, to judge who is the king of the Germans, and to lead the Latin Church to a new crusade. Rome is one of the five great sees of the old church, with Constantinople, Alexandria, Antioch and Jerusalem. Since the split of 1054 Rome and Constantinople do not share the altar, and each says that it is the true church.
The sparks of the war

Four fires burn in 1200. In April 1199 King Richard died, and the claim of his nephew Arthur of Brittany stands against his brother John. In 1198 the princes of Germany elected two kings, Philip of Swabia and Otto of Brunswick. In 1198 Innocent called a new crusade, and the great lords of France and Flanders took the cross. In January 1200 the pope laid an interdict on France, because King Philip put away his Danish queen. Any one of these fires can burn the whole map.

Philip Augustus wants Normandy, Anjou and the rest of the land that the English kings hold in France. He fears the pope, who has laid an interdict on his kingdom, and he fears an alliance of John with the Welf party and Flanders. His first goal is a peace that makes John his vassal, and a wedding of his son Louis to Blanche of Castile.

John holds the lands of his father and of his brother, but the lords of Anjou, Maine and Touraine back his nephew Arthur. He wants to keep every land and to keep the money of England flowing to the war. He fears Philip Augustus most. His first goal is a peace with France, and then the safety of Aquitaine through his mother Eleanor and a new marriage.

Raymond VI rules a rich land where the Cathar faith grows, and where Jews, Catholics and heretics live next to each other. He wants his land to stay free of Paris, Rome and Aragon. He fears the legates of Innocent III, who ask him to hunt the heretics. His first goal is to keep peace with his vassals and to avoid a war with the Church.

Peter II holds Aragon, Catalonia and strong rights in the south of France. He wants to bind the counts of Languedoc to his crown and to win glory against the Almohads. He fears that Castile and Navarre close him in. His first goal is to keep peace with his neighbours in Spain, and to ask the pope for a royal crown.

Alfonso VIII lost the battle of Alarcos in 1195, and he wants his revenge. His wife Eleanor is a sister of Richard and John, and he claims Gascony as her dowry. He fears the Almohad army and the kings of Leon and Navarre, who attack when he is weak. His first goal is to heal the army and to unite the Christian kings.

Alfonso IX rules the west of Spain. He wants to be free of the pressure of Castile, and to win land from the Muslim south. He married his cousin Berengaria of Castile, and the church condemned the marriage. He fears an attack by Castile and the anger of the pope. His first goal is to keep his borders and to find an ally.

Sancho I won Silves from the Muslims in 1189 and lost it again in 1191. He wants to settle his land and to push the border south again. He fears the Almohad army, which burned towns of the Tagus. His first goal is to build castles and to settle new towns along the border.

Muhammad al-Nasir is the caliph of Marrakesh, and his army is the largest of the west. He wants the end of the Banu Ghaniya in Ifriqiya and in Majorca, and the end of the Christian kings of Spain. He fears an alliance of those kings, because the pope calls them to a crusade. His first goal is to free Ifriqiya and to gather a great army for Spain.

The Banu Ghaniya are the last family of the Almoravid lords. They hold the Balearic islands and fight in Ifriqiya, and they raid the coast from their ships. They want to hold Tunis and Bejaia and to stay out of the reach of the Almohads. They fear the army of the caliph. Their first goal is to hold the cities that they have won.

Philip of Swabia is the king that the Hohenstaufen party elected in 1198. He wants the crown of the empire and the lands of his dead brother Henry VI. He fears the party of Otto and the money of England. His first goal is to win the cities of the Rhine and to make peace with the pope.

Otto of Brunswick was elected by the lords of the Rhine and crowned in Aachen in 1198. He wants to take the crown from Philip of Swabia, with the help of his uncle John of England. He fears the south of Germany, where the Staufer are strong. His first goal is to win the pope as a friend.

Frederick II is a child of five, king of Sicily since 1198. His mother Constance died in that year, and the pope is his guardian. The lords of the realm want to rule in his name. German captains such as Markward of Anweiler hold lands in the south of Italy. His first goal is to grow up and to keep the island kingdom whole.

Ottokar I rules Bohemia, and in 1198 Philip of Swabia gave him the title of king. He wants to make the title his own for ever, and to keep his land out of the war of the two German kings. He fears the dukes of Austria and Poland. His first goal is to pick the side that pays more.

The papal state holds the land around Rome, and Innocent III wants all of it back. He wants the Holy Land freed and the kings of Europe at his feet. He fears the German captains in Italy and a king of the Germans who is too strong. His first goal is to take back the towns of the papal state and to start the crusade.

Enrico Dandolo is the doge of Venice. He is very old and almost blind, and his mind is sharp. Venice wants the trade of the east and the sea of the Adriatic. It fears Genoa and Pisa and the cities of the Dalmatian coast. Its first goal is to sell ships to the crusade, because only Venice has a fleet for it.

Baldwin IX rules Flanders and Hainaut, rich lands with wool and cloth. He wants back the towns of Artois that Philip Augustus holds. He took the cross in February 1200. He fears the king of France and the debts of a long journey. His first goal is to prepare his land and his knights for the crusade.

Canute VI rules a strong kingdom of the Baltic. His sister Ingeborg married Philip Augustus in 1193, and the king sent her away. Canute wants his sister to be queen again. He fears the German princes in the south and the Slavs in the east. His first goal is to take the case of his sister to the pope.
